summary_zh: 去年，当《平价医疗法案》医疗保险的联邦补贴到期时，佛罗里达州受到的打击尤其严重。现在，随着选举和开放
body_en: The Healthcare Election: Florida When federal subsidies for Affordable Care Act health insurance expired last year, Florida was hit particularly hard. Now, as the election and open enrollment coincide, healthcare is a major issue.
When federal subsidies for Affordable Care Act health insurance expired last year, Florida was hit particularly hard. Now, as the election and open enrollment coincide, healthcare is a major issue.

When federal subsidies and Affordable Care Act healthcare plans expired last year, Florida was hit especially hard. This weekend, as open enrollment begins just days before Election Day, Floridians who use the healthcare exchange are learning what their new premiums are. On average, they're going up 10.4%, according to the state's Office of Insurance Regulation. NPR's Maham Javaid went to a competitive congressional district in Florida, spanning from the Gulf Coast to the suburbs of Palm Beach, to find out if rising healthcare insurance costs are moving votes.

MAHAM JAVAID, BYLINE: Bordering Naples Beach are palm trees and pastel-colored mansions. Brittany Garcia (ph), a 23-year-old registered nurse, is walking the shore after an overnight shift. Garcia has no health insurance.
BRITTANY GARCIA: I would hope that there is some reform soon because I literally have no access to healthcare.

JAVAID: She works as a contractor, so Garcia wants to buy insurance on the healthcare marketplace. Those are plans under the Affordable Care Act, also known as Obamacare. Premiums are rising as COVID-19-era subsidies have expired. For many like Garcia, healthcare has become unaffordable.
GARCIA: I started looking and nothing was available, so I couldn't buy insurance. And to me, that was scary. You know, it made me think maybe I have to go to another country.
JAVAID: Garcia has previously voted Republican. Now, without access to insurance, she's not sure how she will vote.
GARCIA: This time, I'm just voting with my convictions.

JAVAID: The newly redrawn 22nd Congressional District sprawls across south Florida. Made up of rural, urban and suburban areas, it's home to wealthy communities and working-class families. Politically, it swings between red and blue. Northeast of Naples, Collier County is a diverse area, home to immigrants from Haiti, Mexico and Guatemala. This is where Bianca (ph) and her husband live. They've been without insurance since January. That's when her insurance agent called and said...

BIANCA: But I do want to let you know that because they're going to take away the subsidy, that it's now going to be this amount of money. And at the time, I think it was, like, doubled or tripled of what we were paying.

JAVAID: She's had to pay out of pocket for an emergency visit to the hospital and pneumonia treatment. Bianca asked NPR not to use her full name because political activists in her community have faced harassment for speaking up. She's going to vote for the Democratic nominee, Pia Dandiya, and her reason is healthcare.

BIANCA: She is trying to expand the Affordable Care Act, which I think is really important, especially for, like, families like mine and my husband, where we're working 40 hours a week, and we can't afford healthcare.
ROHIT DANDIYA: Nice to meet you. I'm Pia's father.
JAVAID: On the western edge of the district, Dandiya's father welcomes us into her campaign office.
R DANDIYA: Here. Come on in. Hello. Pia, are you here?
JAVAID: If Democrats were to win back the House, Dandiya says she's going to work on restoring ACA subsidies, expanding funding to Medicaid and lowering drug prices.
P DANDIYA: Healthcare is not a blue issue or a red issue. It's a red, white and blue issue. It's something that is impacting all of us.
JAVAID: Her Republican opponent, Casey Askar, wants to eliminate the ACA altogether and crack down on fraud to preserve Medicare and Medicaid. His campaign did not reply to interview requests.

The district is home to many retirees and veterans who often vote for Republicans. Several of those we spoke to express satisfaction with the healthcare options they already have, including Medicare and private insurance. But Dandiya says the district she's running in doesn't lean either way.
body_zh: 医疗保健选举：佛罗里达州 当《平价医疗法案》医疗保险的联邦补贴去年到期时，佛罗里达州受到的打击尤其严重。现在，随着选举和公开招生的同时进行，医疗保健成为一个主要问题。
去年，当《平价医疗法案》医疗保险的联邦补贴到期时，佛罗里达州受到的打击尤其严重。现在，随着选举和公开招生的同时进行，医疗保健成为一个主要问题。

去年，当联邦补贴和《平价医疗法案》医疗保健计划到期时，佛罗里达州受到的打击尤其严重。本周末，随着公开注册在选举日前几天开始，使用医疗保健交换的佛罗里达人正在了解他们的新保费是多少。根据该州保险监管办公室的数据，保险费平均上涨 10.4%。 NPR 的马哈姆·贾维德 (Maham Javaid) 前往佛罗里达州一个竞争激烈的国会选区，从墨西哥湾沿岸一直延伸到棕榈滩郊区，以了解不断上涨的医疗保险成本是否正在影响选票。
马哈姆·贾维德连线：那不勒斯海滩边有棕榈树和色彩柔和的豪宅。 23 岁的注册护士布列塔尼·加西亚（Brittany Garcia，博士）上完夜班后正在海边散步。加西亚没有健康保险。
布列塔尼·加西亚：我希望尽快进行一些改革，因为我实际上无法获得医疗保健。
JAVAID：她是一名承包商，因此加西亚想在医疗保健市场上购买保险。这些是《平价医疗法案》（也称为奥巴马医改法案）下的计划。随着 COVID-19 时代的补贴到期，保费正在上涨。对于像加西亚这样的许多人来说，医疗保健已经变得难以负担。
加西亚：我开始寻找，但没有任何可用的东西，所以我无法购买保险。对我来说，这很可怕。你知道，这让我觉得也许我必须去另一个国家。
贾维德：加西亚此前曾投票支持共和党。现在，由于无法获得保险，她不确定自己将如何投票。
加西亚：这一次，我只是根据我的信念投票。
贾维德：新重新划定的第 22 国会选区横跨佛罗里达州南部。它由农村、城市和郊区组成，是富裕社区和工薪阶层家庭的家园。政治上，它在红色和蓝色之间摇摆。科利尔县位于那不勒斯东北部，是一个多元化的地区，是来自海地、墨西哥和危地马拉的移民的家园。这是比安卡（博士）和她丈夫居住的地方。他们自一月份以来就没有保险。就在那时，她的保险代理人打电话来说……
比安卡：但我确实想让你知道，因为他们将取消补贴，所以现在将是这笔钱。当时，我认为它是我们所支付费用的两倍或三倍。
贾维德：她必须自掏腰包去医院紧急就诊并支付肺炎治疗费用。比安卡要求 NPR 不要使用她的全名，因为她所在社区的政治活动人士因发声而受到骚扰。她将投票给民主党候选人皮亚·丹迪亚（Pia Dandiya），她的理由是医疗保健。
比安卡：她正在努力扩大《平价医疗法案》，我认为这非常重要，特别是对于像我和我丈夫这样的家庭，我们每周工作 40 个小时，而且我们负担不起医疗费用。
罗希特·丹迪亚： 很高兴认识你。我是皮娅的父亲。
贾维德：在该区的西边，丹迪亚的父亲欢迎我们来到她的竞选办公室。
R DANDYA： 在这里。进来吧。你好。皮娅，你在吗？
贾维德：丹迪亚表示，如果民主党要赢回众议院，她将致力于恢复平价医疗法案补贴、扩大医疗补助资金并降低药品价格。
P DANDYA：医疗保健不是蓝色问题或红色问题。这是一个红、白、蓝的问题。这是影响我们所有人的事情。
JAVAID：她的共和党对手凯西·阿斯卡 (Casey Askar) 希望完全废除 ACA 并打击欺诈行为，以维护医疗保险和医疗补助。他的竞选团队没有回复采访请求。
该地区是许多退休人员和退伍军人的家园，他们经常投票给共和党。我们采访的一些人对他们已有的医疗保健选择表示满意，包括医疗保险和私人保险。但丹迪亚表示，她竞选的选区并不偏向任何一方。

title_en: Politics, norms and the DOJ's unprecedented pre-election headlines
title_zh: 政治、规范和司法部前所未有的选前头条新闻
summary: The Justice Department, contrary to past norms, has stayed in the headlines in the run-up to the midterm election.
summary_zh: 与过去的惯例相反，司法部在中期选举前夕一直是头条新闻。
body_en: Politics, norms and the DOJ's unprecedented pre-election headlines : NPR
Politics, norms and the DOJ's unprecedented pre-election headlines The Justice Department, contrary to past norms, has stayed in the headlines in the run-up to the midterm election.
Politics, norms and the DOJ's unprecedented pre-election headlines
The Justice Department, contrary to past norms, has stayed in the headlines in the run-up to the midterm election.

The U.S. Justice Department has been busy recently filing cases, investigating President Trump's perceived enemies, and filing election-related lawsuits against certain states, as the midterm elections approach. NPR Justice correspondent Ryan Lucas joins us. Ryan, thanks so much for being with us.
RYAN LUCAS, BYLINE: Thanks for having me, Scott.

LUCAS: Well, look, we have certainly seen a flurry of politically charged cases and investigations by the Justice Department over the past month. There was the search by federal agents at the home of Democratic Congresswoman Ilhan Omar, who's one of Trump's fiercest critics in Congress. That search was part of an investigation into possible immigration fraud. We've also seen two former FBI officials charged in connection with the investigations into former President Biden's son, Hunter Biden.

And James Comey, the former FBI director, also was charged this month for allegedly leaking sensitive information 10 years ago. That is the third criminal case against Comey in little over a year, if you're keeping track. And last but not least, prosecutors tried and failed just this week to secure a grand jury indictment against a former Trump White House aide who had provided damning testimony to House lawmakers about the January 6 Capitol riot.
SIMON: A long list of prominent names of people who've been critical of the president. How unusual is it to see the Justice Department do this so close to an election?

LUCAS: It's not normal at all, Scott. In fact, the department has a long-standing practice that has been observed by both Republican and Democratic administrations over the years that the department does not take overt investigative actions in the two months or so before an election, and it doesn't do that so that it avoids even the possibility of being seen as interfering or influencing an election.

There's, in fact, even a section in the Justice Department's internal rulebook, so to speak, that says prosecutors and agents can never do anything with the purpose of affecting an election. And critics, including legal experts, department veterans, say the department's recent actions are clear violations. Attorney General Todd Blanche has pushed back on that. Here's what he said when asked about it earlier this month.

TODD BLANCHE: When we have to execute a search warrant or an arrest, if there's a crime that occurs, we take into consideration the purpose and making sure the purpose is proper, which is what the Justice Manual requires, and that's what we did then, and that's what we do in every case.
SIMON: Ryan, please tell us about the lawsuits the Justice Department filed in California and Alaska over the elections.

LUCAS: Right. So in the California lawsuit, the Justice Department wants the state to set aside any vote by mail ballots associated with a list of 20,000 names that the DOJ says are likely noncitizens until the voters' citizenship has been verified. This week, a federal judge and an appeals court rejected that request, but the Justice Department hasn't backed down in the broader fight over the state's voter rolls because, on Thursday, it sent out grand jury subpoenas to California election officials, and that is seen as a significant escalation on the Justice Department's part.

LUCAS: Yeah. That's been a wild ride. So this is a lawsuit that President Trump has said he told the Justice Department to file. The department wants the court to delay certification in the U.S. Senate race in Alaska if the Republican incumbent, Dan Sullivan, loses by a small margin. That's because there's another Dan Sullivan on the ballot, and the argument is that having two people with the same name could confuse voters. The state's Supreme Court already ruled that both Sullivans could run.

Things seemed to have settled down until a New York Times report this week that said Democrats recruited the second Dan Sullivan to run specifically to siphon votes away from the Republican. The Justice Department revised its lawsuit to include those allegations. Alaska's governor has ordered an investigation. The Justice Department already has a criminal investigation underway, so there's certainly going to be more to come on that front.
SIMON: NPR Justice correspondent Ryan Lucas, thanks so much.

政治、规范和司法部前所未有的选前头条新闻 与过去的规范相反，司法部在中期选举前夕一直成为头条新闻。
政治、规范和司法部前所未有的选前头条新闻
与过去的惯例相反，司法部在中期选举前夕一直是头条新闻。
随着中期选举的临近，美国司法部最近忙于立案，调查特朗普总统的敌人，并对某些州提起与选举相关的诉讼。 NPR 司法记者瑞安·卢卡斯 (Ryan Lucas) 加入我们。瑞安，非常感谢您和我们在一起。
瑞安·卢卡斯连线：谢谢你邀请我，斯科特。
卢卡斯：嗯，看，过去一个月我们确实看到了司法部一系列带有政治色彩的案件和调查。联邦特工对民主党众议员伊尔汗·奥马尔 (Ilhan Omar) 的家进行了搜查，她是特朗普在国会最激烈的批评者之一。这次搜查是对可能的移民欺诈调查的一部分。我们还看到两名前联邦调查局官员因调查前总统拜登的儿子亨特·拜登而受到指控。
前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米本月也因涉嫌 10 年前泄露敏感信息而受到指控。如果你留意的话，这是一年多来针对科米的第三起刑事案件。最后但并非最不重要的一点是，检察官本周试图让大陪审团对特朗普前白宫助手提出起诉，但未能成功，这名助手曾就 1 月 6 日国会大厦骚乱向众议院议员提供了令人震惊的证词。
西蒙：一长串批评总统的名人。司法部在临近选举时这样做有多不寻常？
卢卡斯：这根本不正常，斯科特。事实上，该部门有一个多年来共和党和民主党政府都遵循的长期做法，即在选举前两个月左右的时间里，该部门不会采取公开的调查行动，这样做甚至避免了被视为干预或影响选举的可能性。
事实上，司法部的内部规则手册中甚至有一部分可以说，检察官和特工永远不能做任何以影响选举为目的的事情。包括法律专家、部门资深人士在内的批评者表示，该部门最近的行为明显违法。司法部长托德·布兰奇对此进行了反驳。以下是他本月早些时候被问及此事时的说法。
托德·布兰奇：当我们必须执行搜查令或逮捕时，如果发生犯罪，我们会考虑目的并确保目的正确，这是《司法手册》的要求，也是我们当时所做的，也是我们在每个案件中所做的。
西蒙：瑞安，请告诉我们司法部在加利福尼亚州和阿拉斯加就选举提起的诉讼。
卢卡斯：对。因此，在加利福尼亚州的诉讼中，司法部希望该州搁置与司法部认为可能是非公民的 20,000 名名单相关的任何邮寄选票，直到选民的公民身份得到验证为止。本周，一名联邦法官和一家上诉法院拒绝了这一请求，但司法部并没有在有关该州选民名册的更广泛斗争中退缩，因为周四，它向加州选举官员发出了大陪审团传票，这被视为司法部方面的重大升级。
卢卡斯：是的。那真是一次疯狂的旅程。这是特朗普总统表示他要求司法部提起的诉讼。如果共和党现任议员丹·沙利文以微弱优势落败，该部门希望法院推迟对阿拉斯加美国参议院竞选的认证。这是因为选票上还有另一个丹·沙利文，而争论的焦点是两个人同名可能会让选民感到困惑。该州最高法院已经裁定两名沙利文都可以参选。
事情似乎已经尘埃落定，直到《纽约时报》本周报道称，民主党招募了第二任丹·沙利文来专门竞选，以从共和党手中夺走选票。司法部修改了诉讼以纳入这些指控。阿拉斯加州州长已下令进行调查。司法部已经展开刑事调查，因此这方面肯定还会有更多调查。
西蒙：NPR 司法记者瑞安·卢卡斯 (Ryan Lucas)，非常感谢。

title_zh: 政治一周：特朗普的中西部支点；更尖锐的民主信息
summary: The president heads to the midwest for two rallies he previously said were cancelled. Has his message changed this campaign season and how have Democrats sharpened their messaging?
summary_zh: 总统前往中西部参加他先前所说已取消的两次集会。他的信息在这个竞选季节发生了变化吗？民主党有何变化？
body_en: Week in Politics: Trump's Midwest pivot; sharper Democratic messaging : NPR

Week in Politics: Trump's Midwest pivot; sharper Democratic messaging The president heads to the midwest for two rallies he previously said were cancelled. Has his message changed this campaign season and how have Democrats sharpened their messaging?
Week in Politics: Trump's Midwest pivot; sharper Democratic messaging
The president heads to the midwest for two rallies he previously said were cancelled. Has his message changed this campaign season and how have Democrats sharpened their messaging?

And late last night, a federal judge in California slapped back at the Justice Department with an order that it may not threaten, intimidate or coerce any state or local elections officials or workers over counting ballots. Some confusion this week with President Trump's schedule. He originally planned to wrap up his midterm election campaigning with rallies this weekend in Kansas and Iowa. On Thursday, he announced he wasn't going - instead would do tele-rallies. But now Kansas and Iowa are back on the president's schedule. NPR's Ron Elving joins us. Ron, thanks for being with us.
RON ELVING, BYLINE: Good to be with you, Scott.
SIMON: Do we know why these weekend rallies were initially scrapped?

ELVING: No, not for certain. President Trump said Friday night that his phone blew up after the Iowa, Kansas cancellations. People were very disappointed, and Trump said he did not want to let them down. We do know a lot of the scheduling is being driven by data analysis, but was there something else? One theory is that the cancellations had generated some kind of a buzz that Trump didn't like, suggestions that he was throwing in the towel in those races in those states. And these are two Senate seats now in Republican hands that the party badly needs to hold, especially Kansas, where no Democrat has been elected to the Senate since 1932.

SIMON: President spent last month going from one battleground state to another. But he has been campaigning since early September, in that first-ever Republican National Midterm Convention. Has his message changed at all?

ELVING: Only here and there at the margins. Mostly it's about the securing of the southern border and various claims about the economy that are at odds with most voters with what most voters, at least, say they are seeing themselves. That includes the tariffs and inflation and surging gas prices and other things Trump says will just go away right after the election. Lately, he's been stressing his case on Democrats cheating. That includes his accusations of noncitizens voting with no evidence beyond a handful of cases.

He's seized on a New York Times report we just heard about. Alaska Democrats had been looking for people named Dan Sullivan to get on the ballot against incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan. But the printed ballot clearly differentiates between the two Sullivans, makes clear that one of them is the incumbent senator. And the Alaska Supreme Court has already taken a look at this case, and the Alaska ranked-choice system simply allows more than one candidate from a single party.
SIMON: Look, we've both learned to be cautious about polls. Right now, it does seem that candidate quality still matters.

ELVING: The Democrats have been outspent. They're battling almost limitless resources from Republican donors such as Elon Musk. Multiple sources say that he has spent over $350 million on this cycle overall. So the Democrats hope that voters will still be able to get information and that that information will be about people who could have run for Congress on their lives outside of politics. Many of them did. Those candidates defy the stereotypes of Democrats as being coastal elites. So, for example, in Kansas, where Trump's arriving this weekend, the Democrats' nominee, Adam Hamilton, is an ordained Methodist minister. And in Texas, the Democratic Senate candidate, James Talarico, has been studying for a divinity degree at a Presbyterian seminary and is the grandson of a Baptist minister.
SIMON: Ron, what are you going to be watching for Tuesday night?

ELVING: All the usual things - turn out, of course, who jumps out to an early lead, which races get called early, which look likely to be undecided. And by the way, those undecided may be undecided for days to come. But this year, with all of Trump's threats, I think we'll be watching as well for interference in various forms, both on Election Day and night and in the days to come. And it's not likely to be over on election night or even the next day.
SIMON: And for more of NPR's sharp political analysis, you can check out the 2026 election tab on the NPR app. It's at npr.org/2026election.

总统前往中西部参加他先前所说已取消的两次集会。他的信息在这个竞选季节是否发生了变化？民主党人如何强化他们的信息？
昨晚深夜，加利福尼亚州的一名联邦法官回击司法部，下令司法部不得在计票过程中威胁、恐吓或胁迫任何州或地方选举官员或工作人员。本周特朗普总统的日程安排有些混乱。他原本计划本周末在堪萨斯州和爱荷华州举行集会来结束中期选举竞选活动。周四，他宣布他不会去，而是举行电话集会。但现在堪萨斯州和爱荷华州又回到了总统的日程上。 NPR 的 Ron Elving 加入我们。罗恩，谢谢你和我们在一起。
罗恩·埃尔文连线：很高兴和你在一起，斯科特。
西蒙：我们知道为什么这些周末集会最初被取消吗？

埃尔文：不，不确定。特朗普总统周五晚上表示，爱荷华州和堪萨斯州的航班取消后，他的手机发生了爆炸。人们非常失望，特朗普表示他不想让他们失望。我们确实知道很多调度是由数据分析驱动的，但是还有其他原因吗？一种理论认为，取消选举引起了特朗普不喜欢的某种轰动，有人认为他在这些州的竞选中认输了。这两个参议院席位现在掌握在共和党手中，该党急需保住，尤其是堪萨斯州，该州自 1932 年以来就没有民主党人当选参议员。
西蒙：总统上个月从一个战场州到另一个战场州。但他自九月初以来一直在参加有史以来第一次共和党全国中期代表大会上的竞选活动。他的信息有改变吗？
ELVING：仅在边缘的一些地方。主要是关于南部边境的安全以及有关经济的各种主张，这些主张与大多数选民至少表示他们对自己的看法不一致。这包括关税、通货膨胀、飙升的汽油价格以及特朗普所说的其他事情将在选举后立即消失。最近，他一直在强调民主党作弊的情况。这包括他对非公民在没有证据的情况下投票的指控，除了少数案件。
他抓住了我们刚刚听到的《纽约时报》的一篇报道。阿拉斯加民主党一直在寻找丹·沙利文（Dan Sullivan）的人来投票反对现任共和党参议员丹·沙利文（Dan Sullivan）。但打印的选票清楚地区分了两位沙利文，明确表明其中一位是现任参议员。阿拉斯加州最高法院已经审理了此案，而阿拉斯加州的排名选择制度只是允许来自一个政党的多名候选人。
西蒙：看，我们都学会了对民意调查持谨慎态度。目前看来，候选人的质量确实仍然很重要。

埃尔文：民主党的开支已经超出了。他们正在与埃隆·马斯克等共和党捐助者的几乎无限的资源作斗争。多个消息来源称，他在这个周期上总共花费了超过 3.5 亿美元。因此，民主党希望选民仍然能够获得信息，并且这些信息将是关于那些可以在政治之外竞选国会议员的人的信息。他们中的许多人都这么做了。这些候选人打破了民主党人作为沿海精英的刻板印象。例如，在特朗普本周末抵达的堪萨斯州，民主党提名人亚当·汉密尔顿 (Adam Hamilton) 被任命为卫理公会牧师。在得克萨斯州，民主党参议员候选人詹姆斯·塔拉里科(James Talarico)一直在长老会神学院攻读神学学位，他是浸信会牧师的孙子。
西蒙：罗恩，周二晚上你打算看什么？
ELVING：所有常见的事情 - 当然，结果是谁一早就领先，哪些比赛被提前宣布，哪些比赛看起来可能尚未决定。顺便说一句，那些犹豫不决的人可能会在未来几天内犹豫不决。但今年，鉴于特朗普的所有威胁，我认为我们还将关注各种形式的干扰，无论是在选举日、选举之夜还是在未来几天。而且它不太可能在选举之夜甚至第二天就结束。

title_en: El-Sayed campaign wants Stevens to stay away after day of back-and-forth sniping
title_zh: 埃尔赛义德竞选团队希望史蒂文斯在一天的来回狙击后远离
summary: Some Democrats worry that the blowup between the two former primary rivals is imperiling their hold on the seat.
summary_zh: 一些民主党人担心，这两个前初选竞争对手之间的冲突正在危及他们对席位的掌控。
body_en: TRAVERSE CITY, MICHIGAN — Michigan's Democratic coalition is fragmenting in real time days before a critical Senate election.

After it seemed like former primary rivals Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens might finally appear together, they’re back to sniping at each other. And it could hardly come at a worse moment as Democrats look to unite behind El-Sayed and hold on to a pivotal Senate seat.

El-Sayed’s campaign is asking Stevens to stay away from all future campaign events in the closing days of the race, two people familiar with the decision, who were granted anonymity to discuss sensitive campaign dynamics, told POLITICO.
She should stay away “as not to distract from the central issues of the campaign,” one of the people said.

The brushoff capped a day of the two lobbing increasingly pointed statements back and forth at each other, frustrating Democrats who say the infighting risks imperiling a state the party can hardly afford to lose as they try to flip control of the Senate.

“I have no idea what the hell Haley Stevens is doing. This is a moment where we have to recognize the stakes,” Michigan state Sen. Mallory McMorrow, who was squeezed out of the Democratic primary by the two other candidates, told CNN earlier on Friday, before El-Sayed issued his response. “People are not talking about ads. They are not talking about Haley Stevens. They are talking about the price of gas and groceries.”

Stevens did not immediately respond to a question on if she will now stay off the trail, and did not respond to an earlier question about whether her appearance was contingent on him apologizing. El-Sayed’s campaign declined to comment.

El-Sayed narrowly defeated Stevens in a bitter and hard-fought primary in August that exposed division over support for Israel. The seat now held by the retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters is crucial to Democratic hopes to take control of the Senate.
Stevens and El Sayed have not campaigned together since a post-primary unity breakfast, but appeared on the verge of doing so earlier on Friday.
Stevens initially said she would appear alongside El-Sayed and South Carolina Rep. Jim Clyburn at a church in Detroit on Sunday.

But she said she expected the Democratic nominee to apologize for some of his past comments and condemn an ad run by an outside group supporting him that she described as antisemitic. The ad featured a conversation in a grocery store where a woman told a man they couldn't buy eggs because they had to set aside money for “killing Palestinians.” El-Sayed’s campaign had previously noted he was not affiliated with the ad.

In response, El-Sayed did not touch on the ad or his past comments on Israel, instead saying that his campaign “has always been focused on addressing the most critical challenges Michiganders are facing” and that that focus “is why our people-powered campaign defeated a historic $70 [million] in outside spending from big corporations and AIPAC on behalf of Congresswoman Stevens.”
“So while Congresswoman Stevens seems intent on relitigating a primary that ended three months ago, let’s all focus on the task at hand: that’s beating Mike Rogers,” El-Sayed said.
Privately, Democrats are frustrated — some with Stevens.

“Every Democrat was singing the same tune but now, because one person is tone deaf, the whole choir is thrown off,” said a Michigan Democratic operative who is not directly working for El-Sayed’s campaign.
Some Democrats tried to downplay the fight heading into the final days of the race.

“There’s been a lot of efforts to coalesce Democrats, both from Abdul and from the congresswoman. I think everybody's on the same page of Democrats just beating Mike Rogers," said Joe Tate, a state representative from Detroit who supported Stevens in the primary and is now backing El-Sayed. But he acknowledged that "when you have people that have competed through a primary, I know it can always have those lingering effects."
Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg urged Democrats to come together to support El-Sayed.

“I've never met somebody who I agree with on 100 percent of everything,” Buttigieg told reporters while campaigning in the state for House candidate Callie Barr on Friday. “But when our health care is at stake, when a chance to have a more affordable everyday life is at stake, the choice is clear: Mike Rogers has disqualified himself.”

Republicans have sought to play up the Democratic divisions. Rogers, in a Friday evening post on X , called Stevens a “courageous leader” and said she was “absolutely right” to call on El-Sayed to apologize.
body_zh: 密歇根州特拉弗斯城——在关键的参议院选举前几天，密歇根州的民主党联盟正在分裂。
在前主要竞争对手阿卜杜勒·赛义德和众议员海莉·史蒂文斯似乎最终可能一起出现后，他们又开始互相攻击。民主党人希望团结起来支持埃尔赛义德并保住关键的参议院席位，这真是再糟糕不过的时刻了。
两名知情人士告诉《政治》杂志，埃尔-赛义德的竞选团队要求史蒂文斯在比赛最后几天远离所有未来的竞选活动。两位知情人士被要求匿名讨论敏感的竞选动态。
其中一位知情人士表示，她应该远离“以免分散对竞选核心问题的注意力”。
这次拒绝结束了两人互相发表越来越尖锐的言论的一天，这让民主党人感到沮丧，他们表示，在试图扭转参议院控制权时，内讧可能会危及该党难以承受失去的一个州。
“我不知道海莉·史蒂文斯到底在做什么。现在是我们必须认识到其中利害关系的时刻，”被另外两名候选人挤出民主党初选的密歇根州参议员马洛里·麦克莫罗周五早些时候告诉美国有线电视新闻网，随后埃尔·赛义德发表了回应。 “人们不是在谈论广告。他们不是在谈论海莉·史蒂文斯。他们是在谈论汽油和杂货的价格。”
史蒂文斯没有立即回答关于她现在是否会远离踪迹的问题，也没有回答早些时候关于她的出现是否取决于他道歉的问题。埃尔赛义德的竞选团队拒绝发表评论。
八月份，埃尔-赛义德在一场激烈的初选中以微弱优势击败了史蒂文斯，暴露了在支持以色列问题上的分歧。目前由即将退休的民主党参议员加里·彼得斯 (Gary Peters) 担任的席位对于民主党控制参议院的希望至关重要。
史蒂文斯和埃尔·赛义德自初选后团结早餐后就没有一起竞选，但周五早些时候似乎即将一起竞选。
史蒂文斯最初表示，她将于周日与埃尔-赛义德和南卡罗来纳州众议员吉姆·克莱伯恩一起出现在底特律的一座教堂。
但她表示，她希望这位民主党候选人能够为自己过去的一些言论道歉，并谴责一个支持他的外部团体投放的广告，她称该广告是反犹太主义的。该广告以杂货店里的一段对话为特色，一名妇女告诉一名男子，他们不能买鸡蛋，因为他们必须留出钱来“杀害巴勒斯坦人”。埃尔-赛义德的竞选团队此前曾指出，他与该广告无关。
作为回应，埃尔-赛义德没有提及这则广告或他过去对以色列的评论，而是表示他的竞选活动“一直专注于解决密歇根人面临的最严峻的挑战”，而这一重点“就是为什么我们以人民为动力的竞选活动代表国会女议员史蒂文斯击败了大公司和 AIPAC 历史性的 7000 万美元外部支出。”
“因此，虽然国会女议员史蒂文斯似乎有意重新提起三个月前结束的初选，但让我们都专注于手头的任务：击败迈克·罗杰斯，”埃尔赛义德说。
私下里，民主党人感到沮丧——有些人对史蒂文斯感到沮丧。
“每个民主党人都在唱同样的调子，但现在，因为一个人五音不全，整个唱诗班都被抛弃了，”一位不直接为埃尔赛义德竞选活动工作的密歇根州民主党工作人员说。
一些民主党人在竞选最后几天试图淡化这场斗争。
“阿卜杜勒和女议员都为团结民主党做出了很多努力。我认为每个人都同意民主党击败迈克·罗杰斯，”底特律州众议员乔·泰特说，他在初选中支持史蒂文斯，现在又支持埃尔·赛义德。但他承认，“当有人参加过初选时，我知道它总是会产生挥之不去的影响。”
前交通部长皮特·布蒂吉格敦促民主党人团结起来支持埃尔·赛义德。
“我从来没有遇到过在所有事情上都百分百同意的人，”布蒂吉格周五在该州为众议院候选人卡莉巴尔竞选时告诉记者。 “但是，当我们的医疗保健受到威胁时，当获得更实惠的日常生活的机会受到威胁时，选择就很明确了：迈克·罗杰斯已经取消了自己的资格。”
共和党人一直试图渲染民主党的分歧。罗杰斯在周五晚上的《X》上发表文章，称史蒂文斯是一位“勇敢的领导人”，并表示她要求埃尔赛义德道歉是“绝对正确的”。

title_en: Judge dismisses Trump’s $10 billion defamation suit over Epstein birthday card story
title_zh: 法官驳回特朗普因杰弗里·爱泼斯坦生日贺卡故事提出的 100 亿美元诽谤诉讼
summary: A federal judge in Florida has tossed a revised version of President Donald Trump’s $10 billion defamation suit against The Wall Street Journal over a story about a birthday card he allegedly sent Jeffrey Epstein more than two decades ago.
summary_zh: 佛罗里达州一名联邦法官驳回了唐纳德·特朗普总统针对《华尔街日报》提起的价值 100 亿美元的诽谤诉讼的修改版。
body_en: Judge dismisses Trump’s $10 billion defamation suit over Jeffrey Epstein birthday card story

A federal judge in Florida has tossed a revised version of President Donald Trump’s $10 billion defamation suit against The Wall Street Journal over a story about a birthday card he allegedly sent Jeffrey Epstein more than two decades ago.

U.S. District Judge Darrin Gayles found Trump’s amended suit suffered from the same fatal flaw as his first attempt — it fell far short of the high legal bar to show the paper had published the story with “actual malice.”

“As President Trump has not plausibly alleged that each Defendant made defamatory statements with actual malice, the Amended Complaint must be dismissed. And because this is President Trump’s second attempt to allege his claims, the Court finds that dismissal with prejudice is appropriate,” the judge wrote.

Trump first sued the paper last July , shortly after the Journal published a story about a birthday book that Ghislaine Maxwell had assembled for Epstein’s 50th birthday in 2003. The book appeared to include a card from Trump, who had been friends with Epstein around that time.

The card contained a hand-drawn outline of a naked woman with what appeared to be Trump’s first name signed in the pubic area. It included a typewritten note depicting an imaginary conversation with Epstein, who would later be charged with sex trafficking.
Trump denied having anything to do with the card, and his suit accused the paper of having made it up and that no such note existed.
Epstein’s estate later released a copy of a card matching the Journal’s description. Trump and the White House maintain the document is a fake.

Trump’s suit alleged the writers of the article “falsely represent as fact that President Trump drew the naked woman’s breasts and signed his name ‘Donald’ below her waist, ‘mimicking pubic hair,’” and that the article caused him “overwhelming financial and reputational harm.”

Trump’s suit also criticized the paper for not publishing an image of the card in the initial story, saying that shows “no authentic letter or drawing exists” — even though the House Oversight Committee publicly released the card after getting it from the Epstein estate.

The suit says the Journal should have known the story was bogus because Trump said it was not true. It also chided the paper for failing to interview Epstein co-conspirator Maxwell, who’s serving 20 years in prison on sex trafficking charges. The story said Journal reporters wrote her a letter asking for an interview and included a comment from her attorney.

The paper’s attorneys argued that like the original suit, Trump’s revised suit came “nowhere close” to demonstrating the paper acted with actual malice, in which “the false statement was made with knowledge that it was false or with reckless disregard of whether it was false or not.”

Despite Trump’s claim the paper failed to properly investigate the card before publishing the story, “the Article itself established that the Journal not only investigated” but also “informed readers that President Trump decried the Letter as a fake and denied writing it,” the paper said in its motion to dismiss the suit.
Further, the attorneys argued, alleging that someone sent another person a birthday card is not defamatory.

“There is nothing inherently defamatory about sending a bawdy letter to a friend,” the attorneys wrote, and the article “emphasizes that the Birthday Book was created before Epstein was first arrested” and “makes clear that President Trump’s friendship with Epstein ended years before Epstein was charged with sex crimes.”
The attorneys also contended the suit should be dismissed because the public release of the card shows the story was “substantially true.”
In an interview last year with then-Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche, Maxwell acknowledged assembling the birthday book but said she could not remember whether Trump contributed to it.

The White House maintains the signature is not Trump’s and that it looks different from his distinctive full signature. Democrats compiled a number of documents where Trump signed just his first name over the year, and the signatures appear very similar to the one on the card.

body_zh: 法官驳回特朗普因杰弗里·爱泼斯坦生日贺卡故事提出的价值 100 亿美元的诽谤诉讼
佛罗里达州一名联邦法官驳回了唐纳德·特朗普总统对《华尔街日报》提起的 100 亿美元诽谤诉讼的修改版，该诉讼涉及他据称在二十多年前寄给杰弗里·爱泼斯坦的一张生日贺卡。
美国地区法官达林·盖尔斯（Darrin Gayles）发现，特朗普修改后的诉讼与他的第一次尝试存在同样的致命缺陷——它远远没有达到表明该报以“真正的恶意”发表这篇报道的严格法律标准。
法官写道：“由于特朗普总统并没有合理地指控每名被告都怀着真正的恶意发表了诽谤性言论，因此必须驳回修订后的起诉书。而且由于这是特朗普总统第二次尝试指控他的主张，法院认为有偏见地驳回是适当的。”
去年7月，特朗普首次起诉该报，当时《华尔街日报》发表了一篇关于吉斯莱恩·麦克斯韦(Ghislaine Maxwell)在2003年为爱泼斯坦50岁生日准备的一本生日书的报道。这本书似乎包括一张来自特朗普的卡片，特朗普当时是爱泼斯坦的朋友。
这张卡片上有一个手绘的裸体女人轮廓，公共区域签有特朗普的名字。其中包括一张打字纸条，描述了与爱泼斯坦的一次想象中的对话，爱泼斯坦后来被指控犯有性交易罪。
特朗普否认与这张卡片有任何关系，他的诉讼指控该报纸捏造了这张卡片，并且不存在这样的纸条。
爱泼斯坦的遗产管理机构后来发布了一张与《华尔街日报》的描述相符的卡片副本。特朗普和白宫坚称该文件是假的。
特朗普的诉讼称，这篇文章的作者“错误地表述了特朗普总统画了裸体女人的胸部，并在她腰部下方签下自己的名字‘唐纳德’的事实，‘模仿了阴毛’”，并且这篇文章给他造成了“巨大的经济和声誉损失”。
特朗普的诉讼还批评该报没有在最初的报道中发布该卡片的图像，称这表明“不存在真实的信件或图画”——尽管众议院监督委员会在从爱泼斯坦庄园获得该卡片后公开发布了该卡片。
该诉讼称，《华尔街日报》应该知道这个故事是假的，因为特朗普说这不是真的。它还指责该报未能采访爱泼斯坦的同谋麦克斯韦尔，后者因性交易指控而在监狱服刑 20 年。报道称，《华尔街日报》记者给她写了一封信，要求接受采访，其中包括她律师的评论。
该报的律师辩称，与最初的诉讼一样，特朗普修改后的诉讼“远未”证明该报的行为具有真正的恶意，其中“虚假陈述是在明知其虚假的情况下做出的，或者不顾一切地无视其是否虚假”。
该报在驳回诉讼的动议中表示，尽管特朗普声称该报在发表这篇报道之前未能对这张卡片进行适当的调查，但“这篇文章本身表明，该报不仅进行了调查”，而且“告知读者，特朗普总统谴责这封信是伪造的，并否认写了这封信”。
此外，律师还辩称，声称某人向他人发送生日贺卡并不构成诽谤。
律师们写道：“向朋友发送一封淫秽的信本身并没有什么诽谤性的。”文章“强调生日书是在爱泼斯坦首次被捕之前创作的”，并且“明确表明特朗普总统与爱泼斯坦的友谊在爱泼斯坦被指控性犯罪的几年前就结束了。”
律师还认为，该诉讼应该被驳回，因为该卡片的公开发布表明该故事“基本上是真实的”。
去年，在接受时任副司法部长托德·布兰奇采访时，麦克斯韦承认自己组装了这本生日书，但表示她不记得特朗普是否对此做出了贡献。

title_en: Judge tosses Trump lawsuit against WSJ, Murdoch over Epstein story
title_zh: 法官驳回特朗普因爱泼斯坦故事而对《华尔街日报》和默多克提起的诉讼
summary: A federal judge on Saturday threw out President Trump's lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and Rupert Murdoch over the paper's reporting on Trump's ties to Jeffrey Epstein, Why it matters: It's the second time this year courts have blocked Trump's efforts
summary_zh: 周六，一名联邦法官驳回了特朗普总统针对《华尔街日报》和鲁珀特·默多克因该报报道特朗普而提起的诉讼
body_en: A federal judge on Saturday threw out President Trump's lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and Rupert Murdoch over the paper's reporting on Trump's ties to Jeffrey Epstein
Why it matters: It's the second time this year courts have blocked Trump's efforts to sue the paper over stories about his relationship with the disgraced financier.
As with the first one, courts found the president did not clear the high bar set by New York Times vs. Sullivan for allegations of defamation in critical reporting on public figures.

Driving the news: Judge Darrin Gayles of the southern district of Florida issued the 20-page ruling Saturday afternoon, finding that Trump failed to prove the paper acted with "actual malice" by reporting on his links to Epstein.
Gayles dismissed the amended complaint with prejudice, meaning it can't be refiled.
Zoom out: Trump first filed suit against the paper and Murdoch in July 2025, seeking $20 billion in damages.
At issue was a story describing a "bawdy" letter, bearing Trump's name and given to Epstein for his birthday, which the president insisted was fake.

Gayles tossed the initial suit last April, but allowed Trump to file an amended complaint — which was the one he dismissed Saturday, saying it fell short of the burden to prove the paper acted maliciously.

What they're saying: "Indeed, the allegations regarding malice are conclusory, vague, sometimes inconsistent with the Article, and often irrelevant to whether Defendants knew or should have known that the statements in the Article were purportedly false," Gayles wrote.

For the record: " President Trump will continue to press forward in his powerhouse lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal and all of the other defendants. The President will continue to hold those who mislead the American People with Fake News and smears accountable for their actions," a spokesman for his legal team said in a statement.
Editor's note: This story has been updated with additional details.
body_zh: 周六，一名联邦法官驳回了特朗普总统对《华尔街日报》和鲁珀特·默多克的诉讼，因为该报报道了特朗普与杰弗里·爱泼斯坦的关系
为什么重要：这是法院今年第二次阻止特朗普因报道他与这位名誉扫地的金融家的关系而起诉该报的努力。
与第一起案件一样，法院发现总统没有达到《纽约时报》诉沙利文案中针对公众人物批评性报道中诽谤指控设定的高标准。
推动新闻发展：周六下午，佛罗里达州南区法官达林·盖尔斯 (Darrin Gayles) 发布了长达 20 页的裁决，裁定特朗普未能证明该报报道他与爱泼斯坦的联系是出于“真正的恶意”。
盖尔斯带着偏见驳回了修改后的申诉，这意味着该申诉无法重新提交。
缩小：特朗普于 2025 年 7 月首次对该报和默多克提起诉讼，寻求 200 亿美元的赔偿。
争议的一个故事描述了一封带有特朗普名字的“淫秽”信件，是送给爱泼斯坦的生日礼物，但总统坚称这封信是假的。
盖尔斯去年四月驳回了最初的诉讼，但允许特朗普提交一份修改后的投诉——他周六驳回了这一投诉，称该投诉不足以证明该报存在恶意行为。
他们的说法：“事实上，有关恶意的指控是结论性的、模糊的，有时与文章不一致，而且通常与被告是否知道或应该知道文章中的陈述据称是虚假的无关，”盖尔斯写道。
郑重声明：“特朗普总统将继续推进针对《华尔街日报》和所有其他被告的强力诉讼。总统将继续追究那些利用假新闻和诽谤误导美国人民的人的行为，”他的法律团队发言人在一份声明中表示。
编者注：这个故事已经更新了更多细节。

title_en: Judge orders an inquiry into potential DOJ misconduct in Trump's golf course case
title_zh: 法官下令对司法部在特朗普高尔夫球场案中潜在的不当行为进行调查
summary: A federal judge is opening an formal inquiry into Trump officials' conduct in the East Potomac case, including whether they misled the court about their plans for the municipal golf course.
summary_zh: 一名联邦法官正在对特朗普官员在东波托马克案中的行为展开正式调查，包括他们是否在有关案件方面误导了法院。
body_en: Judge orders an inquiry into potential DOJ misconduct in Trump's golf course case
Workers remove downed trees from the East Potomac golf course on Monday. Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP hide caption

WASHINGTON, D.C. — A federal judge is launching a formal inquiry into potential misconduct by Trump administration officials in the lawsuit over East Potomac Park, including whether they repeatedly misrepresented the president's plans for the municipal D.C. golf course.

District Judge Ana Reyes ordered Friday's hearing — the third in as many weeks — to seek clarity from government lawyers days after they acknowledged in writing Wednesday that there is a plan to transform the municipal golf course into a championship-level venue, closing it and much of the surrounding park in mid-November.

For months, Justice Department attorneys representing the Interior Department and National Park Service had maintained in court filings and hearings that such a plan was not yet final, despite President Trump's social media statements proclaiming otherwise.
A judge halted D.C. golf course renovations. Trump says they'll still start next month

Their abrupt confirmation on Wednesday night prompted Reyes to call both sides back into court, just days after she ordered a halt to tree-clearing and major renovations at the park (which the government promptly appealed).

Reyes opened Friday's hearing by quoting the D.C. Bar Rule of Professional Conduct 3.3 , which prohibits lawyers from knowingly making or failing to correct false statements to the court. She asked Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward Jr., who is leading the government's defense, whether there was anything he would like to correct.
"Not to my knowledge," Woodward said, explaining that he hasn't read every transcript in the case. "We have lots of binders," he said, to which Reyes replied: "I bet you do."
Stanley Woodward, the third-highest ranking official at the Justice Department — pictured in 2023 — clashed repeatedly with Judge Ana Reyes at Friday's hearing. Lynne Sladky/AP hide caption

Over the next four hours, Reyes grilled Woodward about the timing and status of the administration's renovation plans. She demanded to know whether officials had not been truthful when they told her last Monday that they were not aware of the park closure that Trump had posted about that same morning.
Reyes called the lawyers' claims into doubt for two main reasons.

Government lawyers acknowledged for the first time in their Wednesday filing that the administration is closing the park next month, both for golf course renovations and to address the man-made peninsula's crumbling seawall. And they said in court that they submitted those renovation plans to the National Capital Planning Commission for review on Friday.

Under questioning, Woodward told the judge that the submission had been in the works for several weeks. But, as Reyes fired back incredulously, no one from the government mentioned that in the previous hearings, one of which lasted seven hours.
Judge chastises Trump administration plan to push ahead overhaul of DC golf course

"Am I to understand that for weeks someone has been putting pen to paper on a submission to design the golf course … while this litigation was ongoing, while Department of Justice employees were representing to me that there was no plan?" she said.

The hearing ended with Reyes announcing that she would "open a formal inquiry into whether agency officials and employees, including agency attorneys and [Justice Department] attorneys, have made misrepresentations to the court and otherwise violated applicable ethical rules."

Reyes said that inquiry may be led by a special master, whom she has not yet appointed but described as a judicial officer with "full investigatory powers." Reyes said if the government rejects her special master, she will conduct the inquiry herself.
Reyes stressed that the opening of an investigation does not mean that the court has found or will find evidence that any government lawyers have violated their professional obligations.

But the relatively unusual move suggests that the judge is finished taking the administration at its word, as she said she has done since local historic preservation advocates and golfers first filed suit in February.
body_zh: 法官下令对司法部在特朗普高尔夫球场案中潜在的不当行为进行调查
周一，工人们从东波托马克高尔夫球场清除倒下的树木。朱莉娅·德玛丽·尼金森/美联社隐藏标题栏
华盛顿特区——一名联邦法官正在对特朗普政府官员在东波托马克公园诉讼中可能存在的不当行为展开正式调查，包括他们是否一再歪曲总统对华盛顿特区高尔夫球场的计划。
地区法官安娜·雷耶斯 (Ana Reyes) 下令在周五举行听证会（这是几周内的第三次听证会），要求政​​府律师澄清事实。几天前，政府律师以书面形式承认，有计划将市政高尔夫球场改造成锦标赛级场馆，并于 11 月中旬关闭该球场及周边公园的大部分区域。
几个月来，代表内政部和国家公园管理局的司法部律师在法庭文件和听证会上坚称，这一计划尚未最终确定，尽管特朗普总统在社交媒体上发表了相反的声明。
法官叫停了华盛顿特区高尔夫球场的翻修工程。特朗普称他们仍将在下个月开始
周三晚上，他们的突然确认促使雷耶斯将双方重新告上法庭，就在几天前，她下令停止公园的树木清理和重大整修（政府立即提出上诉）。
雷耶斯在周五的听证会开始时引用了华盛顿特区律师协会职业行为规则 3.3，该规则禁止律师故意向法庭做出或未能纠正虚假陈述。她询问负责政府辩护的副司法部长小斯坦利·伍德沃德（Stanley Woodward Jr.）是否有任何需要纠正的地方。
“据我所知，”伍德沃德说，并解释说他还没有阅读该案的所有笔录。 “我们有很多活页夹，”他说，雷耶斯回答说：“我打赌你有。”
司法部第三高级别官员斯坦利·伍德沃德（摄于 2023 年）在周五的听证会上与法官安娜·雷耶斯多次发生冲突。琳恩·斯拉基/美联社隐藏标题栏
在接下来的四个小时里，雷耶斯向伍德沃德盘问政府改造计划的时间和状态。她要求知道，官员们上周一告诉她，他们不知道特朗普当天早上发布的公园关闭消息时，他们是否说谎了。
雷耶斯对律师的说法表示怀疑，主要原因有两个。
政府律师在周三提交的文件中首次承认，政府将于下个月关闭该公园，一方面是为了高尔夫球场翻新，另一方面是为了解决人造半岛摇摇欲坠的海堤问题。他们在法庭上表示，他们已于周五将这些改造计划提交给国家首都规划委员会审查。
在接受询问时，伍德沃德告诉法官，提交的材料已经准备了几周。但是，当雷耶斯难以置信地回击时，在之前的听证会上，政府没有人提到这一点，其中一场听证会持续了七个小时。
法官严厉谴责特朗普政府推动华盛顿特区高尔夫球场检修的计划
“我是否可以理解，几周来有人一直在提交一份高尔夫球场设计方案……而诉讼仍在进行中，而司法部员工向我表示没有计划？”她说。
听证会结束时，雷耶斯宣布她将“对机构官员和员工，包括机构律师和[司法部]律师，是否向法院做出虚假陈述以及其他违反适用道德规则的行为展开正式调查。”
雷耶斯表示，调查可能由一名特别负责人领导，她尚未任命该负责人，但称该负责人是一名拥有“全面调查权力”的司法官员。雷耶斯表示，如果政府拒绝她的特别主人，她将亲自进行调查。
雷耶斯强调，展开调查并不意味着法院已经发现或将会发现任何政府律师违反其职业义务的证据。
但这一相对不寻常的举动表明，法官不再相信政府的话，正如她所说，自当地历史保护倡导者和高尔夫球手于二月份首次提起诉讼以来，她一直在这样做。

title_en: Heidi Klum reveals a giant severed hand as 2026 Halloween costume
title_zh: 海蒂·克拉姆 (Heidi Klum) 展示一只巨大的断手作为 2026 年万圣节服装
summary: The TV personality went viral in 2022 when she arrived at a party encased in a slithering worm costume.
summary_zh: 2022 年，这位电视名人穿着蠕动的蠕虫服装参加一个聚会，引起了广泛关注。
body_en: Heidi Klum reveals a giant severed hand as 2026 Halloween costume - CBS News

Heidi Klum underwent a bloody transformation to become a giant, gruesome severed hand for her annual Halloween party in New York on Saturday, 25 years after she began hosting the much-anticipated event.

Klum was unrecognizable, with only her eyes and mouth showing, blood dripping from her mouth as she stuck her tongue out. The top of the hand ended in a gory assortment of dangling ligaments and tendons. She had an ensemble of helpers in blood-stained hazmat suits.
The idea came to her last year to be a giant hand - specifically her own left hand, with long red nails, a thumb ring, and her engagement ring and wedding band.
"I looked at my hand and I thought, 'Hey, I think I could fit my body in this somehow,'" Klum said.
The supermodel-turned-TV personality went viral in 2022 when she arrived at the party on the end of a fishing line, encased in a slithering worm costume.

In past years, Klum has come dressed as the Greek myth Medusa, a peacock, an 8-foot-tall (2.4-meter-tall) "Transformer," a werewolf from Michael Jackson's "Thriller" music video, a clone accompanied by several Klum-lookalikes, and Kali, the multiarmed Hindu goddess of death and destruction.

Klum said it took about five to six hours to get into her hand costume this year, but making it took a lot longer. She posted hints on her Instagram earlier in the day as bloodied prosthetics were applied to her face.
"Hands down, the hardest thing is carrying it," Klum said. "It's quite heavy."

Her husband, musician Tom Kaulitz, did not attend this year because he was on tour. But the details on her costume include a tattoo of his name on her ring finger, along with her palm lines and veins.

body_zh: 海蒂·克鲁姆 (Heidi Klum) 展示了一只巨大的断手作为 2026 年万圣节服装 - 哥伦比亚广播公司 (CBS) 新闻

克鲁姆已经面目全非，只露出眼睛和嘴巴，伸出舌头时，鲜血从嘴里滴下来。手的顶部是各种各样悬而未决的血淋淋的韧带和肌腱。她有一群身穿血迹斑斑的防护服的助手。
去年，她萌生了制作一只巨手的想法——特别是她自己的左手，长着长长的红色指甲，拇指戒指，还有她的订婚戒指和结婚戒指。
“我看着我的手，我想，‘嘿，我想我可以以某种方式让我的身体适合这个，’”克鲁姆说。
这位由超模转型的电视名人在 2022 年走红，当时她穿着一条蠕动的蠕虫服装，拿着一根钓鱼线来到聚会现场。
在过去的几年里，克鲁姆曾打扮成希腊神话中的美杜莎、孔雀、8英尺高（2.4米高）的“变形金刚”、迈克尔·杰克逊的“惊悚片”音乐录影带中的狼人、由几个酷似克鲁姆的人陪伴的克隆人，以及多臂印度教死亡和毁灭女神卡莉。
克鲁姆说，今年她大约花了五到六个小时才穿上她的手工服装，但制作花了更长的时间。当天早些时候，她在自己的 Instagram 上发布了一些暗示，当时她的脸上贴上了血迹斑斑的假肢。
“毫无疑问，最困难的事情就是携带它，”克鲁姆说。 “相当重。”
她的丈夫、音乐家汤姆·考利茨今年没有参加，因为他正在巡演。但她服装上的细节包括她的无名指上纹有他的名字，以及她的手掌纹路和静脉。

title_en: This Sunday, conservative pastors will preach against Democrats’ claims to Christian faith
title_zh: 本周日，保守派牧师将宣讲反对民主党对基督教信仰的主张
summary: Evangelical pastors in key battlegrounds plan to warn their congregants about the danger of voting Democratic — even for Christian leaders.
summary_zh: 关键战场上的福音派牧师计划警告他们的会众投票给民主党的危险——即使对于基督教领袖也是如此。
body_en: When Robert Jeffress takes the pulpit at First Baptist Dallas on Sunday, he’ll give his 16,000 congregants a not-so-subtle message: Beware of false faith.
Jeffress will preach about the Tower of Babel, a topic that shares “some parallels to what's happening in the election,” he said in a recent interview with POLITICO.

“My goal as a pastor is not to get people in the voting booth, but to keep them out of hell,” the archconservative megachurch pastor, televangelist and longtime Republican backer said. Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico, a Presbyterian seminarian, “seems harmless,” Jeffress continued, “but the toxic faith he is preaching will lead people away from heaven, not toward it.”

On Sunday morning, conservative evangelical pastors across the country will be sharing a similar message, with the hope of galvanizing their congregations to support right-wing candidates and causes on Election Day.
But the big difference from recent years: They’ll be preaching against Democrats in four battleground U.S. Senate and House races who’ve made their faith a key part of their campaign message.

Talarico is a few classes short of becoming an ordained minister. Kansas Senate Democratic nominee Adam Hamilton is pastor of the largest United Methodist church in the country. In Iowa, Presbyterian pastor Lindsay James and Lutheran minister Sarah Trone Garriott are running for Congress. All four are in tight races in red territory, according to polls.
They’ve all made their faith an explicit part of their closing message.
“Jesus said, ‘Do unto others as you'd have them do unto you.’ This is really important. All of these things guide us,” Hamilton says in his stump speech.
“I approve this message because my faith teaches me that caring for my neighbor is not optional,” James says in a face-to-camera ad .

It’s a marked deviation from decades of the Democratic Party’s gradual march toward a less religious tone that has matched their increasingly secular voting base , and an effort to win over politically moderate believers who have grown disgruntled with Trump and the Republicans.

These Democrats' campaigns have put the country’s conservative evangelical pastors in unfamiliar territory: needing to convince their congregants that self-described fellow believers deserve their condemnation, not their vote.

“There are some Christians that don’t know how to respond to it, because [the candidates] are using all the same language that we do, but they are advocating for a lot of things that we are not for,” said Josh Bingaman, lead pastor of the First Church Open Bible in Des Moines, Iowa.
Many conservative pastors contend these Democrats are wolves in sheep’s clothing, pointing out disagreements on abortion, same-sex marriage, transgender rights or even the nature of God.
In Wichita, Kansas, Rob Rotola of Word of Life Church will lay out the stakes of the election in his Sunday sermon.

He said he has “no problem” calling Hamilton a false prophet, and imagines when his sermon is through, his congregants will “feel sorry for Adam Hamilton and would pray for him, but would tell their friends where he stands.”

In Iowa, Mike Demastus of Fort Des Moines Church of Christ plans to remind his congregants of “the importance of every single one of us, as believers, to go and vote and be engaged in this process.” He doesn’t include Trone Garriott among those “believers”: “She's a poser and a fake, and most conservative evangelical Christians see through that as quickly as she can say it.”
Bob Vander Plaats, an influential evangelical leader in the state, called Trone Garriott a “dangerous politician” and dismissed James as straying from the true path.

“To hijack Scripture to make it fit your agenda, versus to embrace the comprehensive nature of Scripture to fit God's agenda, that's a very, very risky thing to do,” Vander Plaats said in an interview.

A spokesperson for Talarico pointed to the candidate’s past statements on faith, including his assertion that “when I take on the politicians who are serving themselves and not the people, I’m doing it on biblical grounds.”

Trone Garriott spokesperson Zach Schenkman said that “while others try to divide Iowans and dictate how every Christian should practice their faith, Sarah is focused on showing up to make a difference for her neighbors.”
body_zh: 当罗伯特·杰弗里斯周日在达拉斯第一浸信会讲坛时，他将向他的 16,000 名会众传达一个不那么微妙的信息：谨防虚假信仰。
杰弗里斯将宣讲巴别塔，这个话题“与选举中发生的事情有一些相似之处”，他在最近接受《政治》杂志采访时表示。
“作为一名牧师，我的目标不是让人们进入投票站，而是让他们远离地狱，”这位极端保守的大型教会牧师、电视布道者和共和党的长期支持者说。德克萨斯州民主党参议院候选人、长老会神学院生詹姆斯·塔拉里科“似乎无害”，杰弗里斯继续说道，“但他所宣扬的有毒信仰将引导人们远离天堂，而不是走向天堂。”
周日早上，全国各地的保守派福音派牧师将分享类似的信息，希望激励他们的会众在选举日支持右翼候选人和事业。
但与近年来的最大区别是：他们将在美国参议院和众议院的四场关键竞选中宣讲反对民主党，而民主党已将他们的信仰作为其竞选信息的关键部分。
塔拉里科距离被任命为部长还差几个级别。堪萨斯州参议院民主党候选人亚当·汉密尔顿是该国最大的联合卫理公会教堂的牧师。在爱荷华州，长老会牧师林赛·詹姆斯和路德教会牧师莎拉·特隆·加里奥特正在竞选国会议员。民意调查显示，这四家公司都在红色地区展开激烈竞争。
他们都将自己的信仰作为结束语的明确组成部分。
“耶稣说，‘己所不欲，勿施于人。’这非常重要。所有这些都指导着我们，”汉密尔顿在他的竞选演讲中说道。
“我赞同这个信息，因为我的信仰告诉我，关心我的邻居是不可选择的，”詹姆斯在面对镜头的广告中说道。
这与民主党几十年来逐渐走向宗教色彩淡化的明显背离，以适应其日益世俗化的投票基础，也是为了赢得对特朗普和共和党不满的政治温和派信徒的努力。
这些民主党的竞选活动使该国的保守派福音派牧师陷入了陌生的境地：需要说服他们的会众，自称的信徒同胞应该受到他们的谴责，而不是他们的投票。
“有些基督徒不知道如何回应，因为[候选人]使用的语言与我们相同，但他们提倡的很多事情我们并不支持，”爱荷华州得梅因第一教会开放圣经的首席牧师乔什·宾加曼(Josh Bingaman)说。
许多保守派牧师认为这些民主党人是披着羊皮的狼，指出他们在堕胎、同性婚姻、变性人权利甚至上帝本质上存在分歧。
在堪萨斯州威奇托，生命之道教会的罗布·罗托拉将在周日的布道中阐述选举的利害关系。
他说，他“没有问题”称汉密尔顿为假先知，并想象当他的布道结束时，他的会众会“为亚当·汉密尔顿感到难过，并会为他祈祷，但会告诉他们的朋友他的立场。”
在爱荷华州，得梅因堡基督教会的迈克·德马斯特斯计划提醒他的会众“作为信徒，我们每个人去投票并参与这一过程的重要性”。他没有将特隆·加里奥特列入这些“信徒”之中：“她是一个装腔作势、虚伪的人，大多数保守的福音派基督徒在她说出这句话的时候就很快看穿了这一点。”
该州颇具影响力的福音派领袖鲍勃·范德·普拉茨(Bob Vander Plaats)称特隆·加里奥特为“危险的政客”，并斥责詹姆斯偏离了正确的道路。
“劫持圣经以使其适合你的议程，而不是接受圣经的全面性以适应上帝的议程，这是一件非常非常危险的事情，”范德·普拉茨在接受采访时说。
塔拉里科的一位发言人指出了这位候选人过去关于信仰的言论，包括他的断言：“当我与那些为自己服务而不是为人民服务的政客较量时，我是根据圣经这样做的。”
特隆·加里奥特发言人扎克·申克曼表示，“当其他人试图分裂爱荷华州并规定每个基督徒应该如何实践他们的信仰时，莎拉专注于为邻居带来改变。”

title_en: Kamala Harris urges a 'too big to rig' turnout for the midterms and tees off on Trump
title_zh: 卡玛拉·哈里斯敦促中期选举投票率“太大，无法操纵”，并与特朗普展开对决
summary: Kamala Harris has been campaigning for Democratic candidates across multiple states during the final stretch of the midterm elections
summary_zh: 卡马拉·哈里斯在中期选举的最后阶段一直在多个州为民主党候选人竞选
body_en: Kamala Harris urges a 'too big to rig' turnout for the midterms and tees off on Trump
Kamala Harris has been campaigning for Democratic candidates across multiple states during the final stretch of the midterm elections

ATLANTA -- Two years after Kamala Harris lost the presidential election to Donald Trump , she still delights Democratic donors and activists with jabs against him, saying the Republican is “callous, corrupt and incompetent” and calling him the “decorator in chief” for his White House renovations and gold adornments.
But the former vice president also has plenty to say about what her party, the electorate and the country should do next as she also considers whether to run again.
“This is the moment where we turn that anger into action,” Harris said more than once during a busy schedule in the final stretch of the midterm campaign.

Harris campaigned for candidates across seven states, ending with a recent two-day visit to Georgia. It was, in parts, the kind of nostalgic tour seen from Barack Obama and Bill Clinton — two-term presidents whose last campaigns are behind them — and the barnstorming from potential future contenders such as Govs. Gavin Newsom of California and Andy Beshear of Kentucky or U.S. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York.

As the first Black woman elected to nationwide office, Harris urged fellow Black Americans to “honor the ancestors” with their votes but she also has become unapologetically “transactional” by demanding more from politicians.

Harris, a California senator before joining Joe Biden on the 2020 ticket, also pushed fellow Democrats to govern aggressively and she called for “structural work” that she said was necessary to reinvigorate American democracy: U.S. Supreme Court expansion, statehood for the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico, and reconsideration of the Electoral College.
“I think she’s hitting all the right notes,” said Melinda Johnson, a retired nurse who attended a Fulton County Democratic Party fundraising gala that Harris headlined in Atlanta.

Harris made it to early presidential primary states , including Nevada, New Hampshire and Michigan. She also went to Mississippi, not exactly a hotbed of presidential politics, on behalf of U.S. Senate candidate Scott Colom.
“The South is in play,” she said. “When Democrats invest in the South, we can win in the South.”
'Inexplicable' order probed as cause of train crash that killed at least 69: Official
Inside the hunt for killer of University of North Carolina student found beaten
2 college students found dead after going missing while hiking, police say

In Georgia, Harris delved into civil rights history as she accused the U.S. Supreme Court of “backdoor racism” with its decision to gut the Voting Rights Act and allow Republicans to redraw boundaries for congressional districts that now elect nonwhite lawmakers.

“Ruthlessness” is key, she said at the Democratic dinner in Atlanta. “Not ruthlessness in the sense of cruelty … but in our willingness to use our power to deliver on our commitments.” Democrats, she said, “can no longer let process stand in the way of progress.”
Throughout her stops, Harris nodded implicitly at her loss to Trump.

“You know we’ve been spending the last year and a half, so many of us, going through a range of emotions,” she told students. “Anger, depression, sadness, frustration, a sense of helplessness and powerlessness.”
Warning that Trump could try to meddle in Tuesday's election, she echoed one of the president's own mantras to encourage people to vote.
“In this case,” she said at Atlanta’s Elizabeth Baptist Church, “we just need to turn out in really large numbers that would be too big to rig.”
body_zh: 卡玛拉·哈里斯敦促中期选举投票率“太大，无法操纵”，并与特朗普展开对决
卡马拉·哈里斯在中期选举的最后阶段一直在多个州为民主党候选人竞选
亚特兰大——卡玛拉·哈里斯在总统选举中输给唐纳德·特朗普两年后，她仍然对特朗普进行猛烈抨击，令民主党捐助者和活动人士感到高兴，称这位共和党人“冷酷、腐败和无能”，并称他是白宫翻修和黄金装饰的“首席装饰师”。
但这位前副总统对于她的政党、选民和国家下一步应该做什么也有很多话要说，因为她也在考虑是否再次竞选。
“现在是我们将愤怒转化为行动的时刻，”哈里斯在中期竞选最后阶段的繁忙日程中不止一次地说。
哈里斯在七个州为候选人竞选，最近对佐治亚州进行了为期两天的访问。从某种程度上来说，这是巴拉克·奥巴马(Barack Obama)和比尔·克林顿(Bill Clinton)的那种怀旧之旅——这两位总统的最后一次竞选活动都已结束——以及来自州长等未来潜在竞争者的巡回演讲。加利福尼亚州的加文·纽瑟姆和肯塔基州的安迪·贝希尔或纽约州的美国众议员亚历山大·奥卡西奥-科尔特斯。
作为第一位当选全国公职的黑人女性，哈里斯敦促美国黑人同胞用选票“纪念祖先”，但她也对政客提出更多要求，变得毫无歉意的“交易性”。
在与乔·拜登一起竞选 2020 年总统候选人之前，曾担任加州参议员的哈里斯也敦促民主党同僚积极执政，她呼吁开展“结构性工作”，她说这些工作对于重振美国民主是必要的：美国最高法院的扩建、哥伦比亚特区和波多黎各的建州地位以及重新考虑选举团制度。
“我认为她说得对，”退休护士梅琳达·约翰逊(Melinda Johnson)说，她参加了哈里斯在亚特兰大主持的富尔顿县民主党筹款晚会。
哈里斯进入了早期的总统初选州，包括内华达州、新罕布什尔州和密歇根州。她还代表美国参议院候选人斯科特·科洛姆前往密西西比州，那里并不完全是总统政治的温床。
“南方正在发挥作用，”她说。 “当民主党投资南方时，我们就能在南方获胜。”
“莫名其妙”的命令被调查为造成至少69人死亡的火车事故原因：官方
北卡罗来纳大学学生凶手追捕过程中被发现遭到殴打
警方称，两名大学生在徒步旅行中失踪后被发现死亡
在佐治亚州，哈里斯深入研究了民权历史，指责美国最高法院决定废除投票权法案，并允许共和党重新划定现在选举非白人议员的国会选区的界限，这是“后门种族主义”。
她在亚特兰大的民主党晚宴上表示，“无情”是关键。 “不是残酷意义上的无情......而是我们愿意利用我们的权力来履行我们的承诺。”她说，民主党人“不能再让程序阻碍进步。”
在整个停留过程中，哈里斯因输给特朗普而含蓄地点点头。
“你知道，在过去的一年半里，我们很多人都经历了各种各样的情绪，”她告诉学生们。 “愤怒、沮丧、悲伤、沮丧、无助和无力感。”
她警告特朗普可能会试图干预周二的选举，并呼应了总统自己鼓励人们投票的口号之一。
“在这种情况下，”她在亚特兰大的伊丽莎白浸信会教堂说道，“我们只需要提供大量的人员，但数量太大，无法进行操纵。”

title_en: Nashville chef's date night with football scout turns deadly
title_zh: 纳什维尔厨师与足球球探的约会之夜变得致命
summary: What started out as a special dinner date between Jade Benning, a Nashville chef, and Blaise Taylor, an assistant football scout, at her Nashville apartment ended in her call to a friend — and his call to 911.
summary_zh: 最初是纳什维尔厨师杰德·本宁 (Jade Benning) 和足球助理球探布莱斯·泰勒 (Blaise Taylor) 在她的纳什维尔 apa 进行的一次特别晚餐约会
body_en: On the night of Feb. 25, 2023, outside Vanderbilt Medical Center in Nashville, Tennessee, Blaise Taylor was answering police questions about how a date turned into a medical emergency.
BLAISE TAYLOR (police bodycam): We were together having a date night.
Authorities wanted to know what happened to 24-year-old Jade Benning, who had been rushed to the hospital, arriving unresponsive.
BLAISE TAYLOR (police bodycam): She started not to feel well.

Jade Benning started that night with the hope of strengthening her relationship with Blaise Taylor, then a 26-year-old assistant football scout for the Tennessee Titans. Jade, a professional chef, was planning a special night at her apartment — cooking dinner, to be followed by painting pictures. But as the evening progressed, just minutes after taking selfies, Jade fell ill. Blaise said she was spitting up and shaking — unsure what to do, he first called his father.
Evi Taylor, Blaise's mother, said their children would often contact their father, a college football coach, with medical questions.
Evi Taylor : Being in sports and things, a lot of times, you know, they would go to their dad. … He would be on the field. Like if somebody got hurt, he would be the first one there.
Blaise's call with his dad lasted 30 seconds. He told his son to immediately call 911, which Blaise did.
BLAISE TAYLOR (911 call): I don't know what's happening … She's got spit coming out of her mouth and she's shaking.

EMT responders found Jade lying face down on her bed, with no pulse. She was taken by ambulance to a hospital. By then, Jade's best friend, Nijaiha Jackson, had returned to Jade's apartment, only to learn Jade was unresponsive.
Nijaiha Jackson : She has to be OK. I just saw her an hour ago. (cries)

Just an hour earlier, Jade was her usual lively self. She was known, says her family and friends, for being spirited — traits on display in cheerleading. She was captain of the squad at her high school in Little Rock, Arkansas, and cheered in competitions.
Dennis Browning : Jade was very much a bridge builder.
Dennis Browning, Jade's dad, says she has always been about bringing people together — even her own parents — after her mom, Bridget Benning Burks, and her dad divorced.
Dennis Browning : She was always putting out the fire.
She moved from Little Rock to Nashville, to pursue her career, and her dream of owning a restaurant.
Natalie Morales : When did you start to hear the name Blaise Taylor?
Bridget Benning Burks : It wasn't long after she moved there, she told that she had met this person … And my husband's big into sports so he knew exactly who he was.
Blaise Taylor was well known to people in Arkansas who followed college football. A former standout defensive back and top student, who had earned a scholarship to Arkansas State University.
Evi Taylor : You know, when he got to college … he got his bachelor's and his master's in business in three-and-a-half years while playing football and starting his own nonprofit.
body_zh: 2023 年 2 月 25 日晚，在田纳西州纳什维尔范德比尔特医疗中心外，布莱斯·泰勒正在回答警方关于约会如何变成医疗紧急情况的问题。
BLAISE TAYLOR（警察随身摄像机）：我们一起度过了一个约会之夜。
当局想知道 24 岁的杰德·本宁 (Jade Benning) 发生了什么事，她被紧急送往医院，但已失去知觉。
布莱斯·泰勒（警察随身摄像机）：她开始感觉不舒服。
那天晚上，杰德·班宁 (Jade Benning) 开始了她与布莱斯·泰勒 (Blaise Taylor) 的关系，当时她是田纳西泰坦队 (Tennessee Titans) 26 岁的助理橄榄球球探。杰德是一位专业厨师，她计划在她的公寓度过一个特别的夜晚——做饭，然后画画。但随着夜幕降临，就在自拍几分钟后，杰德就病倒了。布莱斯说她在吐口水，浑身发抖，不知道该怎么办，他先给父亲打电话。
布莱斯的母亲埃维·泰勒说，他们的孩子经常联系他们的父亲，一位大学橄榄球教练，询问医疗问题。
埃维·泰勒：在体育运动之类的事情上，很多时候，你知道，他们会去找他们的父亲。 ……他会在场上。就像如果有人受伤，他会是第一个到达的人。
Blaise 与他父亲的通话持续了 30 秒。他告诉儿子立即拨打 911，布莱斯照做了。
BLAISE TAYLOR（911 电话）：我不知道发生了什么事……她嘴里吐出口水，而且浑身发抖。
急救人员发现杰德脸朝下躺在床上，没有脉搏。她被救护车送往医院。那时，杰德最好的朋友尼贾伊哈·杰克逊回到了杰德的公寓，却发现杰德已经没有反应了。
Nijaiha Jackson：她一定没事。我一小时前才见过她。 （哭声）
就在一个小时前，杰德还是她平时活泼的样子。她的家人和朋友说，她以精力充沛而闻名——这些特质在啦啦队中都有体现。她是阿肯色州小石城高中的队长，并在比赛中为比赛加油。
丹尼斯·布朗宁：杰德是个桥梁建造者。
杰德的父亲丹尼斯·布朗宁表示，在她的母亲布里奇特·本宁·伯克斯和父亲离婚后，她一直致力于将人们聚集在一起，甚至包括她自己的父母。
丹尼斯·布朗宁：她总是在灭火。
她从小石城搬到纳什维尔，追求自己的事业，追求拥有一家餐厅的梦想。
娜塔莉·莫拉莱斯：你什么时候开始听说布莱斯·泰勒这个名字的？
布里吉特·本宁·伯克斯：她搬到那里后不久，她告诉我她遇到了这个人……而且我丈夫非常喜欢运动，所以他很清楚自己是谁。
布莱斯·泰勒在阿肯色州关注大学橄榄球的人们中广为人知。一位前杰出的防守后卫和尖子生，曾获得阿肯色州立大学的奖学金。
埃维·泰勒：你知道，当他上大学时……他在三年半的时间里获得了商业学士和硕士学位，同时踢足球并创办了自己的非营利组织。

title_en: Rioters loot stores in Germany amid cost of living protests
title_zh: 德国因生活成本抗议而暴徒抢劫商店
summary: After a largely peaceful protest, violence broke out between police and demonstrators in Germany.
summary_zh: 在一场基本和平的抗议之后，德国警察和示威者之间爆发了暴力事件。
body_en: Rioters smash, loot storefronts amid cost of living protests in Germany - CBS News
Masked rioters smashed storefronts and looted goods late Saturday in Frankfurt, Germany amid a protest against the rising cost of living.

The largely peaceful demonstrations were led by a youth initiative called "Gen Z regelt" - roughly translated to "Gen Z's got this" - rallied in more than 30 cities "for education, health, climate protection and an affordable life," and against any return of military conscription. Organizers said that tens of thousands participated in the protests across the country, but official figures weren't immediately available.
Tensions peaked in the evening as some groups of protesters refused to disperse, sparking clashes and violence in major cities including Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg.
in Frankfurt's financial hub, masked protesters hurled stones, fireworks and pepper bombs, according to police.

Authorities also said looters stole weapons from a gun store, which were later retrieved. Some rioters also threw Molotov cocktails at police after pummeling them with stones and bottles earlier in the day, Frankfurt police said on X.
In the northern city of Hamburg, some protesters also shot pyrotechnics toward police and burned down barricades. Police responded by using water cannons and tear gas to disperse the crowds.
Earlier in the day, demonstrations had been largely peaceful. In Berlin, young protesters gathered at Brandenburg Gate on Saturday afternoon, demanding more investments in education and housing.

"We call for more money to be invested in social services and education, as well as in climate protection - in short, in our future - because we are the ones who will be affected by this the longest and who will have to live with it," high school student Lara Breitenbach said.
Janelle Schulz, another high school student from Berlin, also said that the authorities had to invest more money in education.
"At my school, the ceiling is collapsing because of water damage, nothing is being done about it, we have a shortage of teachers, the toilets are broken," she said.

body_zh: 德国生活费抗议活动中暴徒砸毁、抢劫店面 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
周六晚，在德国法兰克福，蒙面暴徒砸毁店面并抢劫商品，抗议生活成本上涨。
这场基本上和平的示威活动是由一项名为“Gen Z regelt”的青年倡议发起的——大致翻译为“Z世代得到了这个”——在30多个城市举行集会，“争取教育、健康、气候保护和负担得起的生活”，并反对任何重新征兵的行为。组织者表示，全国各地有数万人参加了抗议活动，但官方数据尚未公布。
晚上，一些抗议者拒绝驱散，紧张局势达到顶峰，在柏林、科隆和汉堡等主要城市引发冲突和暴力。
据警方称，在法兰克福金融中心，蒙面抗议者投掷石块、烟花和胡椒炸弹。
当局还表示，抢劫者从一家枪店偷走了武器，这些武器后来被找回。法兰克福警方 X 表示，当天早些时候，一些骚乱者用石块和瓶子殴打警察后，还向警察投掷燃烧弹。
在北部城市汉堡，一些抗议者还向警察发射烟火并烧毁路障。警方使用高压水枪和催泪瓦斯驱散人群。
当天早些时候，示威活动基本上是和平的。在柏林，年轻的抗议者周六下午聚集在勃兰登堡门，要求对教育和住房进行更多投资。
“我们呼吁在社会服务和教育以及气候保护方面投入更多资金——简而言之，在我们的未来——因为我们将是受此影响最久的人，并且将不得不忍受它，”高中生劳拉·布莱滕巴赫说。
另一位来自柏林的高中生贾内尔·舒尔茨也表示，当局必须在教育方面投入更多资金。
“在我的学校，天花板因水灾而倒塌，但我们没有采取任何措施，我们缺少教师，厕所也坏了，”她说。

title_en: Ads accusing Republican candidates of protecting Epstein fill airwaves in final midterm push
title_zh: 中期选举最后一次宣传中，广播中充斥着指责共和党候选人保护爱泼斯坦的广告
summary: But select Democrats, too, are being accused of having ties to the late sex offender as country prepares to vote In races across the country, Democratic candidates or groups that support them have released ads accusing Republicans of protecting pedophiles by v
summary_zh: 但随着国家准备在全国各地的竞选中投票，民主党人也被指控与已故性犯罪者有联系。
body_en: Ads accusing Republican candidates of protecting Epstein fill airwaves in final midterm push
But select Democrats, too, are being accused of having ties to the late sex offender as country prepares to vote

In races across the country, Democratic candidates or groups that support them have released ads accusing Republicans of protecting pedophiles by voting against legislation to release files related to Jeffrey Epstein .
The ads appear intended to evoke an emotional response by accusing candidates of “protecting” Epstein, a notorious pedophile accused of running a sex-trafficking ring involving minors.

An analysis from CNN found that candidates and outside groups have spent more than $35m on Epstein-related ads. Another from the Washington Post found that Democrats spent more than $40m on Epstein-related ads across six key Senate races.
The Epstein files are a sledgehammer for the US midterms | Katie Phang

In Colorado, ads targeting Republican Jeff Crank note that the lawmaker voted against releasing the Epstein files. In one , the family members of Virginia Giuffre, a woman who survived abuse at the hands of Epstein and died by suicide last year, claim Crank “covered up Epstein’s crimes to protect Donald Trump”.
Ashley Hinson, a Senate candidate in Iowa, was accused of voting to “protect her donors” by refusing to vote to release the Epstein files.
“This week I had to explain to my boys, ‘No, Mom does not protect pedophiles,’” Hinson said in a campaign ad responding to attacks over the Epstein files.

An ad targeting Mike Collins , the Republican running for a Georgia Senate seat, says “Mike Collins voted against releasing the Epstein files even after he knew Epstein’s sex-trafficking operation exploited 14-year-old girls for sex”.
Florida Republican Jimmy Patronis faced an attack from his Democratic opponent, claiming he called investigating Epstein “a waste of his time”.

A spokesperson for Crank’s campaign accused the Epstein-related ad of being “intentionally vague”, in a statement to the Washington Post, because his position was that he would vote against the file’s release until he could be confident that victim information was properly redacted. The campaign also said it was “unfortunate” that his opponent, Jessica Killin, was “preying on a grieving family with the help of the Washington Democrats”.

Crank’s staff invited and met with Giuffre’s family, though Crank himself did not meet with them in person, the New York Times reported. Crank’s campaign also said it offered to meet with Epstein victims before the vote on the legislation.

Last year, Democrats and a select few House Republicans tried to force a vote on the Epstein files through a discharge petition – a procedure used in Congress to bypass the traditional steps of legislation and force a vote on the House floor.

Donald Trump, who knew Epstein in the 1990s and early 2000s, opposed the discharge petition for the files, reversing his campaign promise to increase government transparency. House Republicans largely aligned themselves with him, prompting anger from high-profile Trump voters.

Eventually, under pressure from allies, Trump supported the legislation, giving Republican lawmakers the go-ahead to vote for it. All but one House Republican voted for the Epstein Files Transparency Act.

Many of the ads omit the fact that nearly every House Republican voted to release the Epstein files when the Epstein Files Transparency Act came to the floor, although at that point Trump had agreed to sign the legislation and release the files. Instead, the ads refer to Republicans opposing early attempts to force the legislation to the floor.
Republicans have pointed to this fact when disputing the attack ads.

“Of course I voted to release the Epstein files,” Hinson said in a direct-to-camera ad, accusing her opponent, Josh Turek, of lying. While Hinson voted for the final Epstein Files Transparency Act, she did not sign on to the discharge petition.

Patronis, meanwhile, never called the investigation a “waste of time”, but told a local radio station that while he had “no problem getting everything all released”, the issue was a “massive energy and time suck at the end of the day”.
body_zh: 中期选举最后一次宣传中，广播中充斥着指责共和党候选人保护爱泼斯坦的广告
但随着国家准备投票，部分民主党人也被指控与已故性犯罪者有联系
在全国各地的竞选中，民主党候选人或支持他们的团体发布了广告，指责共和党人投票反对公布与杰弗里·爱泼斯坦有关的文件的立法，从而保护恋童癖者。
这些广告似乎旨在通过指责候选人“保护”爱泼斯坦来引发情感反应，爱泼斯坦是一位臭名昭著的恋童癖者，被指控经营涉及未成年人的性交易团伙。
美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 的一项分析发现，候选人和外部团体在与爱泼斯坦相关的广告上花费了超过 3500 万美元。另一篇来自《华盛顿邮报》的报道发现，在六场关键的参议院竞选中，民主党在与爱泼斯坦相关的广告上花费了超过 4000 万美元。
爱泼斯坦文件是美国中期选举的大锤凯蒂·彭
在科罗拉多州，针对共和党人杰夫·克兰克的广告指出，这位议员投票反对公布爱泼斯坦的文件。在其中一篇文章中，弗吉尼亚·朱弗尔（Virginia Giuffre）的家人声称克兰克“掩盖了爱泼斯坦的罪行以保护唐纳德·特朗普”。弗吉尼亚·朱弗尔是一位在爱泼斯坦的虐待中幸存下来并于去年自杀身亡的妇女。
爱荷华州参议员候选人阿什利·辛森 (Ashley Hinson) 被指控拒绝投票公布爱泼斯坦档案，以“保护她的捐助者”。
“本周我必须向我的孩子们解释，‘不，妈妈不保护恋童癖’，”辛森在回应爱泼斯坦档案攻击的竞选广告中说道。
一则针对竞选佐治亚州参议员席位的共和党人迈克·柯林斯 (Mike Collins) 的广告称，“迈克·柯林斯 (Mike Collins) 投票反对公布爱泼斯坦的文件，即使他知道爱泼斯坦的性交易活动剥削 14 岁女孩进行性交易”。
佛罗里达州共和党人吉米·帕特罗尼斯面临民主党对手的攻击，称他称调查爱泼斯坦“浪费时间”。
克兰克竞选团队的一名发言人在给《华盛顿邮报》的一份声明中指责与爱泼斯坦相关的广告“故意含糊其辞”，因为他的立场是，在他确信受害者信息已被正确编辑之前，他将投票反对发布该文件。竞选团队还表示，他的对手杰西卡·基林“在华盛顿民主党的帮助下对一个悲伤的家庭进行掠夺”，这是“不幸的”。
据《纽约时报》报道，克兰克的工作人员邀请并会见了朱弗雷的家人，但克兰克本人并未亲自与他们会面。克兰克的竞选团队还表示，他们愿意在立法投票前与爱泼斯坦的受害者会面。
去年，民主党人和少数众议院共和党人试图通过释放请愿书强制对爱泼斯坦的文件进行投票——这是国会用来绕过传统立法步骤并强制在众议院进行投票的程序。
唐纳德·特朗普在 20 世纪 90 年代和 2000 年代初认识爱泼斯坦，他反对释放这些文件的请愿书，违背了他提高政府透明度的竞选承诺。众议院共和党人基本上与他保持一致，这引发了备受瞩目的特朗普选民的愤怒。
最终，在盟友的压力下，特朗普支持了这项立法，并允许共和党议员投票支持该法案。除一名众议院共和党人外，所有共和党人都投票支持爱泼斯坦档案透明度法案。
许多广告都忽略了这样一个事实：当《爱泼斯坦文件透明度法案》出台时，几乎所有众议院共和党人都投票决定公开爱泼斯坦的文件，尽管当时特朗普已同意签署该法案并公开这些文件。相反，这些广告提到共和党人反对早期强制立法的尝试。
共和党人在争论攻击性广告时指出了这一事实。
“当然，我投票决定公开爱泼斯坦的文件，”辛森在一则直接对着镜头的广告中说道，指责她的对手乔什·图雷克撒谎。虽然辛森投票支持最终的爱泼斯坦档案透明度法案，但她没有在出院请愿书上签字。
与此同时，帕特罗尼斯从未称这项调查是“浪费时间”，而是告诉当地一家广播电台，虽然他“毫无问题地发布所有内容”，但问题是“最终会消耗大量的精力和时间”。

title_en: Josh Shapiro aims for a strong finish in a campaign with 2028 implications
title_zh: 乔什·夏皮罗 (Josh Shapiro) 的目标是在影响 2028 年的竞选活动中取得优异成绩
summary: The Pennsylvania governor has more at stake Tuesday than other 2028 contenders.
summary_zh: 周二，宾夕法尼亚州州长比其他 2028 年竞选总统面临的风险更大。
body_en: POCONO RACEWAY, Pennsylvania — High up in the starting stand of a famed race track, Josh Shapiro waves a black-and-white checkered flag with an unmistakeable meaning: It’s over.
“We may have a lead, but you're coming down this home stretch. People are nipping at your heels,” the Pennsylvania governor told POLITICO. “You’ve got to run hard.”
Shapiro, the potential 2028 contender and 2024 veepstakes short-lister, does have reasons to be optimistic — and careful.
He’s threatening a double-digit blowout over Stacy Garrity, a candidate backed by President Donald Trump, in the most important swing state in the nation.

None of the other potential 2028 Democratic candidates has more at stake in their own backyard on Tuesday than Shapiro. He doesn’t have California Gov. Gavin Newsom’s map-breaking Proposition 50, designed to beat back the GOP redistricting, nor his platinum email list. He doesn’t have Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker’s billions or Arizona Sen. Mark Kelly’s deep bench of donors or former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg’s large map or the red-state credentials of Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear.

Shapiro is on the brink of flipping four hotly contested congressional seats — and guaranteeing Democrats the House. Pennsylvania Democrats could also take control of the state Senate, including some heavily gerrymandered seats, giving the party a governing trifecta for the first time since 1992.
“I’m not thinking about this as a victory for me,” he told POLITICO during a swing through the state. “I'm thinking about this as a victory for our country.”
All of which paves the way for him to pass a $15 minimum wage and a raft of other measures that could buttress a 2028 presidential bid.

Shapiro is very much following the Ron DeSantis theory of a presidential primary campaign: demonstrate dominance at home before branching out nationally — a strategy, it should be noted, that didn’t pay off for the Florida governor.

“I think what really hurt DeSantis was that he decided he wasn't going to announce until after his legislative session, and that was May,” political strategist David Axelrod said. “Time is at a premium. If that’s his plan, that would be a miscalculation.”
Will we see him venture beyond Pennsylvania’s boundaries before the end of the year?
“I don’t know what my plans are,” Shapiro said.

The day had the feeling of both an ending of one campaign and the beginning of another. Even as he urged a midday audience of about 100 people to vote for Paige Cognetti, the Scranton mayor running against Rep. Rob Bresnahan, and Brian Wrightson, the state Senate candidate challenging Sen. Rosemary Brown, he is nationalizing his rhetoric.

“Don’t let Trump take away your hopefulness,” he told people gathered at East Stroudsburg University. “Don't let him make you feel pessimistic. Don't let him feel like change can't come or that we have to look in the rearview mirror for answers. The answers are always straight ahead.”
Then there’s his set piece about the “American dream slipping away.”
He’s broadening out his message beyond the commonwealth.

“I think the work I do here in Pennsylvania, the confidence I give them about their government here can hopefully restore some of their faith in democracy, and I want in our democracy, and I want them to feel like they've got power to be able to shape the future of that American dream,” Shapiro told us.

A few hours later, Shapiro materializes inside Salerno’s, a tavern in Old Forge known for its American cheese-topped pizza. He sets a room in which patrons already have had a few too many Rolling Rocks and pumpkin martinis abuzz.
On the televisions, his own ad for Wrightson is playing on TV. He grips and grins and backslaps his way through the room.
At the end of the bar, he picks up five pizzas for the road, ducks out the door and boards his bus for another Cognetti rally.
body_zh: 宾夕法尼亚州波科诺赛道——在一条著名赛道的起跑台高处，乔什·夏皮罗挥舞着一面黑白格子旗，其含义不容置疑：一切都结束了。
这位宾夕法尼亚州州长告诉《政治》杂志：“我们可能领先，但你正在冲刺。人们正在追赶你。” “你必须努力奔跑。”
夏皮罗是 2028 年潜在的竞争者和 2024 年副总统竞选的入围者，他确实有理由保持乐观和谨慎。
他威胁要在美国最重要的摇摆州以两位数的优势击败唐纳德·特朗普总统支持的候选人史黛西·加里蒂(Stacy Garrity)。

周二，其他潜在的 2028 年民主党候选人中，没有一个人比夏皮罗在自家后院面临的风险更大。他没有加州州长加文·纽森 (Gavin Newsom) 旨在阻止共和党重新划分选区的突破性的 50 号提案，也没有他的白金电子邮件列表。他没有伊利诺伊州州长 JB Pritzker 的数十亿美元，也没有亚利桑那州参议员 Mark Kelly 的捐助者阵容，也没有前交通部长 Pete Buttigieg 的大地图，也没有肯塔基州州长 Andy Beshear 的红色州资格。
夏皮罗即将推翻四个竞争激烈的国会席位，并保证民主党在众议院的席位。宾夕法尼亚州民主党还可能控制州参议院，包括一些严重不公正划分选区的席位，从而使该党自 1992 年以来首次获得三连胜。
“我并不认为这对我来说是一场胜利，”他在该州巡游时告诉《政治》杂志。 “我认为这是我们国家的胜利。”
所有这些都为他通过 15 美元的最低工资和一系列其他可能支持 2028 年总统竞选的措施铺平了道路。
夏皮罗非常遵循罗恩·德桑蒂斯的总统初选理论：先在国内展现主导地位，然后再向全国扩张——值得注意的是，这一策略并没有为佛罗里达州州长带来回报。
“我认为真正伤害德桑蒂斯的是，他决定要等到立法会议结束后才会宣布这一决定，而那是五月，”政治策略师大卫·阿克塞尔罗德说。 “时间非常宝贵。如果这是他的计划，那将是一个误判。”
我们会在今年年底之前看到他冒险超越宾夕法尼亚州的边界吗？
“我不知道我的计划是什么，”夏皮罗说。
这一天给人的感觉既是一场战役的结束，又是另一场战役的开始。尽管他敦促中午约 100 人投票给斯克兰顿市长佩奇·科涅蒂 (Paige Cognetti) 和布莱恩·赖特森 (Brian Wrightson)，前者与众议员罗布·布雷斯纳汉 (Rob Bresnahan) 竞争，后者则挑战参议员罗斯玛丽·布朗 (Rosemary Brown)，但他正在将自己的言论国有化。
“不要让特朗普夺走你们的希望，”他对聚集在东斯特劳兹堡大学的人们说。 “不要让他让你感到悲观。不要让他觉得改变不可能到来，或者我们必须在后视镜中寻找答案。答案总是直截了当的。”
然后是他关于“美国梦正在消失”的设定。
他正在将自己的信息扩展到英联邦之外。
夏皮罗告诉我们：“我认为我在宾夕法尼亚州所做的工作，我给予他们对这里政府的信心，有望恢复他们对民主的一些信心，我想要我们的民主，我希望他们觉得他们有能力塑造美国梦的未来。”
几个小时后，夏皮罗出现在萨莱诺酒馆内，这是旧福吉的一家小酒馆，以其美式奶酪披萨而闻名。他设置了一个房间，顾客们已经喝了太多滚石乐队和南瓜马提尼酒了。
电视上正在播放他自己为赖特森拍摄的广告。他握紧拳头，咧嘴一笑，拍着背，穿过房间。
在酒吧的尽头，他买了五个披萨准备路上吃，然后溜出门，登上巴士去参加另一场科涅蒂集会。

body_en: Vote Republican, or else: How Trump is dangling government help on the campaign trail - ABC News
Vote Republican, or else: How Trump is dangling government help on the campaign trail
President Donald Trump is signaling to states that his administration may be far less likely to help if their voters put Democrats in power on Election Day

WASHINGTON -- President Donald Trump says Georgia GOP Senate candidate Mike Collins can call him whenever he wants to ask for help for his state. But if Georgia reelects Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff, Trump says it could be another story.

“There’s a big difference between that and Pee-wee Herman calling,” Trump said last week in Perry, Georgia, using his derisive nickname for Ossoff. The president acted out a hypothetical scenario at his rally where Ossoff called to ask for money for his state, with Trump responding, “I don’t give a damn what he wants.”

It’s been a recurring theme at Trump’s rallies this month: From North Carolina to Ohio to Kansas , the president has dangled the idea that his administration would be far less likely to help states where Democrats win in the upcoming midterm elections.

Trump has sandwiched the threats into rallies where he has announced goodies like new semiconductor investments, a submarine repair center and fewer limits on a certain type of diesel, underscoring to the audience the types of tangibles an all-Republican Washington could continue to deliver for voters should his party remain in power after November.

But the president’s utterances — part of a larger political strategy that’s anchored on making the midterms about himself and activating conservative voters — have also injected politics into processes that have traditionally remained apolitical, such as doling out disaster aid and providing benefits for veterans.

“It’s a losing strategy for the failed president to insult and threaten voters while he’s in town reminding them he made everything more expensive,” Ossoff told The Associated Press in response to Trump’s rally comments in Perry.

Asked for further elaboration on the pattern of remarks, the White House said Trump is committed to keeping a Republican majority in Congress so “he can continue to deliver on his winning, commonsense agenda.”

White House spokesman Davis Ingle cited Trump’s policies on taxes, prescription drugs, immigration and other policies and added, “Democrats have made it clear that they have no agenda to improve the lives of the American people.”
Yet some of Trump’s remarks have handed ammunition to Democratic candidates in key battleground races.

A sweeping 2022 veterans law signed by then-President Joe Biden allowed those facing health conditions linked to contaminated water at Camp Lejeune , a Marine Corps base in North Carolina, to file for compensation.

In Greenville, North Carolina, earlier this month, Trump announced that $1 billion in cash settlements had been delivered to veterans and their family members who had been affected by the Lejeune contamination, and that he would direct the Justice Department to settle all remaining legitimate claims expeditiously — “if we win the House and the Senate.”
“So, if we don’t win, there’s no money,” Trump said. “If we do win, you’re getting it.”

Questioned afterward at the White House, Trump said, “If we’re not there, then somebody else is going to have to settle” the Camp Lejeune claims and he “can’t speak for another administration,” although his own Justice Department is handling the claims.

It wasn’t the first time Trump had made that type of remark in North Carolina, where his handpicked Senate candidate, Michael Whatley, has struggled to gain traction against Democrat Roy Cooper, a well-known former governor.

During a September rally in Gastonia, Trump said North Carolina was still waiting on more Hurricane Helene recovery money and added, “Now, if Michael loses, I’m not sending it,” even though he immediately said he was kidding.

Cooper has described Trump’s Camp Lejeune threats as “insulting and frustrating” while his campaign has gone after Whatley for refusing to denounce them. (Whatley, asked in a local television interview about the president's comments, said caring for the affected veterans and families is a priority.)

投票共和党，否则：特朗普如何在竞选过程中晃动政府的帮助
唐纳德·特朗普总统向各州发出信号，如果选民在选举日让民主党掌权，他的政府可能不太可能提供帮助
华盛顿——唐纳德·特朗普总统表示，佐治亚州共和党参议院候选人迈克·柯林斯可以在任何时候为该州寻求帮助时给他打电话。但特朗普表示，如果佐治亚州再次选举民主党参议员乔恩·奥索夫，情况可能会不同。
“这和皮威·赫尔曼的电话有很大的不同，”特朗普上周在佐治亚州佩里说道，他用了他对奥索夫的嘲讽绰号。总统在集会上表演了一个假设场景，奥索夫打电话给他的州索要资金，特朗普回应道：“我才不在乎他想要什么。”
这是特朗普本月集会上反复出现的一个主题：从北卡罗来纳州到俄亥俄州再到堪萨斯州，总统一直在暗示他的政府不太可能帮助民主党在即将到来的中期选举中获胜的州。
特朗普将这些威胁夹在集会上，他宣布了新的半导体投资、潜艇维修中心和减少对某种柴油的限制等好东西，向观众强调，如果他的政党在11月后继续掌权，全共和党的华盛顿可以继续为选民提供有形的东西。
但总统的言论是一项更大的政治战略的一部分，该战略的基础是让中期选举以他自己为中心，并激活保守派选民。他的言论也将政治注入到传统上保持非政治性的进程中，例如发放救灾援助和为退伍军人提供福利。
奥索夫在回应特朗普在佩里的集会言论时告诉美联社：“对于这位失败的总统来说，侮辱和威胁选民是一种失败的策略，他在城里提醒他们，他让一切都变得更加昂贵。”
当被要求进一步阐述言论模式时，白宫表示，特朗普致力于保持共和党在国会的多数席位，以便“他可以继续实现他获胜的、符合常识的议程。”
白宫发言人戴维斯·英格尔引用了特朗普在税收、处方药、移民和其他政策方面的政策，并补充说，“民主党人已经明确表示，他们没有改善美国人民生活的议程。”
然而，特朗普的一些言论为关键战场竞选中的民主党候选人提供了弹药。
时任总统乔·拜登签署的 2022 年全面退伍军人法允许那些因北卡罗来纳州海军陆战队基地勒琼营受污染水而面临健康问题的人申请赔偿。
本月早些时候，特朗普在北卡罗来纳州格林维尔宣布，已向受勒琼污染影响的退伍军人及其家人提供 10 亿美元的现金和解金，并且他将指示司法部迅速解决所有剩余的合法索赔——“如果我们赢得众议院和参议院的席位”。
“所以，如果我们没有赢，就没有钱，”特朗普说。 “如果我们真的赢了，你就得到了。”
随后在白宫接受质询时，特朗普表示，“如果我们不在那里，那么其他人将不得不解决”勒琼营的指控，而他“无法代表另一届政府发言”，尽管他自己的司法部正在处理这些指控。
这并不是特朗普第一次在北卡罗来纳州发表此类言论，他精心挑选的参议院候选人迈克尔·沃特利(Michael Whatley)一直在努力赢得对民主党人、著名前州长罗伊·库珀(Roy Cooper)的支持。
9月份在加斯托尼亚举行的一次集会上，特朗普表示北卡罗来纳州仍在等待更多的飓风海伦恢复资金，并补充道，“现在，如果迈克尔输了，我不会寄钱，”尽管他立即表示自己在开玩笑。
库珀称特朗普的勒琼营威胁是“侮辱和令人沮丧的”，而他的竞选团队则因沃特利拒绝谴责这些威胁而对他进行了攻击。 （沃特利在接受当地电视采访时被问及总统的评论时表示，照顾受影响的退伍军人和家庭是当务之急。）
